s1.syndrome_frame: Pelvic mass with restricted mobility and primary infertility
salient_findings: Large pelvic mass extending from the right adnexa to the left
Bilateral breast nodules suggestive of fibroadenomas
Cervix not visualized due to large firm mass
key_facts: Patient is a 29-year-old female
Patient has primary infertility
Pelvic mass is soft to firm and bosselated
Mass has restricted mobility
Mass extends from the pelvis to the epigastrium
Bilateral breast nodules are suggestive of fibroadenomas
Serum tumor markers are within normal limits
MRI findings suggest an ovarian primary
Histopathology shows a spindle cell tumor
Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse positivity for smooth muscle actin
Genetic testing detected a pathogenic variant in the FH gene

s4.champion: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer

raw.champion: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a large pelvic mass, primary infertility, and bilateral breast nodules, combined with the histopathological findings of a spindle cell tumor and the detection of a pathogenic variant in the FH gene, strongly supports the diagnosis of Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer.

rejected.label: Uterine leiomyoma
rejected.why: The mass is described as arising from the pelvis and extending into the pouch of Douglas, and the uterus is not felt separately from the mass, suggesting an ovarian origin rather than a uterine one.

rejected.label: Ovarian leiomyoma
rejected.why: While the MRI findings suggest an ovarian primary, the presence of a pathogenic variant in the FH gene and the patient's other symptoms suggest a more complex syndrome rather than a solitary ovarian leiomyoma.

rejected.label: Intravenous leiomyomatosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of intravenous growth or other characteristics typical of intravenous leiomyomatosis in the patient's presentation or histopathological findings.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The histopathological findings and immunohistochemistry results do not support a diagnosis of leiomyosarcoma, as the tumor is described as a spindle cell tumor with a diffuse hemangiopericytomatous pattern of vasculature and prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and the MIB-1 labeling index is low (1-5%).
